content.text: Blue-green deployment for orders service: setup, steps, and rollback.

nodes.stableKey: Blue-green deployment for the orders service › How blue-green works § group#0

content.label: How blue-green works
content.takeaway: Blue-green deployments use two identical environments for safe, zero-downtime releases.

nodes.stableKey: Blue-green deployment for the orders service › How blue-green works § text#0

content.markdown: You keep two identical production environments, called blue and green.¹ One of them serves all live traffic while the other sits idle; you deploy the new version to the idle one, test it there, and then move traffic over in one step.² Because the old environment is still running, going back is the same one-step switch.³ The cost is running twice the infrastructure during a release, which is why the idle environment is scaled down between releases.⁴

nodes.title: Notes
nodes.stableKey: Blue-green deployment for the orders service › How blue-green works § text#1

content.markdown:
¹ These environments are identical to ensure consistency.
² This allows for zero-downtime deployments and easy rollback.
³ This is a key benefit of blue-green deployments, enabling rapid recovery from issues.
⁴ Scaling down helps manage costs, but the infrastructure still incurs some expense.

nodes.title: Annotation Value
nodes.stableKey: Blue-green deployment for the orders service › How blue-green works § text#2

content.markdown: The annotations clarify the 'why' and 'how' behind each step of the blue-green deployment process, adding depth to the initial description. They highlight the benefits (zero-downtime, easy rollback) and trade-offs (cost of infrastructure) that are implied but not explicitly stated in the original prose.

nodes.stableKey: Blue-green deployment for the orders service › Before you start § group#0

content.label: Before you start
content.takeaway: Ensure all prerequisites are met before the first release.

nodes.title: Two identical environments are required
nodes.stableKey: Blue-green deployment for the orders service › Before you start § text#0

content.markdown: You need two identical environments, `orders-blue` and `orders-green`, with the same instance count, size, and configuration.

nodes.title: Health endpoint must be available
nodes.stableKey: Blue-green deployment for the orders service › Before you start § text#1

content.markdown: A `GET /healthz` endpoint is required that returns `200` only when the service can reach its database and queue.

nodes.title: Database migrations must be backward compatible
nodes.stableKey: Blue-green deployment for the orders service › Before you start § text#2

content.markdown: Database migrations must be backward compatible, allowing the old version to function with the new schema. Both versions share one database, and a rollback does not undo a migration. If any migration is not backward compatible, do not use this procedure; instead, split the migration into an additive release first and a cleanup release later.

nodes.title: Access to load balancer listener rules is essential
nodes.stableKey: Blue-green deployment for the orders service › Before you start § text#3

content.markdown: You need access to the load balancer's listener rules, as the switch involves changing which target group the listener forwards to.

nodes.title: Error rate monitoring is necessary
nodes.stableKey: Blue-green deployment for the orders service › Before you start § text#4

content.markdown: A dashboard or query showing the 5xx error rate per environment is needed to differentiate errors between green and blue environments.

nodes.stableKey: Blue-green deployment for the orders service › Steps § group#0

content.label: Steps
content.takeaway: Blue/green deployment with rollback points and a 24-hour standby for blue.

nodes.stableKey: Blue-green deployment for the orders service › Steps § shape#0
Blue-green deployment for the orders service › Steps § text#0

content.markdown: Deploy version `2.8.0` to `orders-green` using the same build artifact that passed staging. All green instances should report the new version, and blue should still serve 100% of traffic.

nodes.stableKey: Blue-green deployment for the orders service › Steps § shape#1
Blue-green deployment for the orders service › Steps § text#1

content.markdown: Apply database migrations from the new release once, from a single job. The migration job should exit with code 0, and blue should continue serving requests without new errors, confirming backward compatibility.

nodes.stableKey: Blue-green deployment for the orders service › Steps § shape#2
Blue-green deployment for the orders service › Steps § text#2

content.markdown: Poll the health endpoint on every green instance until all return `200`. If any instance fails health checks after 10 minutes, stop and roll back by tearing down green, leaving blue to serve traffic.

nodes.stableKey: Blue-green deployment for the orders service › Steps § shape#3
Blue-green deployment for the orders service › Steps § text#3

content.markdown: Send the smoke-test suite to green's internal address. All smoke tests must pass. If one fails, treat it as a failed health check and stop.

nodes.stableKey: Blue-green deployment for the orders service › Steps § shape#4
Blue-green deployment for the orders service › Steps § code#0
Blue-green deployment for the orders service › Steps § text#4

content.markdown: Within about 30 seconds, new requests should be served by green, and blue should receive no new connections.

nodes.stableKey: Blue-green deployment for the orders service › Steps § shape#5
Blue-green deployment for the orders service › Steps § text#5

content.markdown: Observe the 5xx error rate on green for 15 minutes. If the error rate rises above 2% at any point, switch back to blue using `$BLUE_TG_ARN` (traffic returns to blue within about 30 seconds). If it stays at or below 2%, continue.

nodes.stableKey: Blue-green deployment for the orders service › Steps § shape#6
Blue-green deployment for the orders service › Steps § text#6

content.markdown: Leave blue running, unchanged, for 24 hours as a rollback target.

nodes.stableKey: Blue-green deployment for the orders service › Steps § shape#7
Blue-green deployment for the orders service › Steps § text#7

content.markdown: After 24 hours without a switch-back, scale blue down. Blue then becomes the idle environment for the next release, with roles reversed.

nodes.title: Initial State
nodes.stableKey: Blue-green deployment for the orders service › Steps § text#8

content.markdown: Blue is live, and green is idle.

nodes.title: Rollback Points
nodes.stableKey: Blue-green deployment for the orders service › Steps § text#9

content.markdown: The process includes explicit rollback points if health checks or smoke tests fail, or if the error rate on green exceeds 2% after traffic switch. These ensure customer impact is minimized.

nodes.title: Outcome
nodes.stableKey: Blue-green deployment for the orders service › Steps § text#10

content.markdown: The new version is deployed to green, traffic is switched, and blue is retired after a 24-hour standby period, becoming the idle environment for the next release.

nodes.stableKey: Blue-green deployment for the orders service › When things go wrong § group#0

content.label: When things go wrong
content.takeaway: Understand rollback implications and avoid migrations on standby.

nodes.title: Rollback before step 5
nodes.stableKey: Blue-green deployment for the orders service › When things go wrong § text#0

content.markdown: Rolling back before step 5 is inexpensive as customers haven't seen the new version yet.

nodes.title: Switch-back after step 5
nodes.stableKey: Blue-green deployment for the orders service › When things go wrong § text#1

content.markdown: Switching back after step 5 is quick, but in-flight requests might fail and require client retries.

nodes.title: Database and backward compatibility
nodes.stableKey: Blue-green deployment for the orders service › When things go wrong § text#2

content.markdown: Neither rollback method reverts the database, emphasizing the importance of backward-compatible migrations.

nodes.title: Record failures
nodes.stableKey: Blue-green deployment for the orders service › When things go wrong § text#3

content.markdown: Always record what caused a failure before retrying, as the same build often fails for the same reason.

nodes.title: Avoid migrations on standby
nodes.stableKey: Blue-green deployment for the orders service › When things go wrong § text#4

content.markdown: Do not run the next release's database migrations while the blue environment is on standby.

nodes.title: Risk of schema incompatibility
nodes.stableKey: Blue-green deployment for the orders service › When things go wrong § text#5

content.markdown: Running migrations on standby can make the standby incompatible with the schema, removing the safe switch-back option.

nodes.title: Tutorial Overview
nodes.stableKey: Blue-green deployment for the orders service § text#0

content.markdown: This tutorial details a blue-green release process for the `orders-api` web service. The process starts from a fresh build and deploys to a cleaned-up environment.

nodes.title: Prerequisites
nodes.stableKey: Blue-green deployment for the orders service § text#1

content.markdown: It is assumed that the `orders-api` service is already operating behind a load balancer.

nodes.title: Summary
nodes.stableKey: Blue-green deployment for the orders service § text#2

content.markdown: This section introduces a tutorial for performing a blue-green deployment of the `orders-api` service. The key aspects covered are the starting state (fresh build) and the target environment (cleaned-up). A prerequisite for this tutorial is an existing load balancer setup for the service.
